article.title: NFL EDGE Sunday Evening Brief
article.dek: Two of the three morning cards won, Mike Evans is back tonight in a 49ers uniform, and Cincinnati keeps climbing toward -6.

items.headline: Correction: Mike Evans is back tonight — for the 49ers
paragraphs: First, a correction from this morning. This morning's brief said Mike Evans was expected back for Tampa Bay. That was wrong. Evans plays for San Francisco, and he returns tonight against Minnesota in Mexico City.
Evans has been out with a flare-up of Achilles tendinitis, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. He leads the 49ers with 70 receiving yards per game over the six games he has played this season.

Tonight is the biggest game left on the Week 11 board: San Francisco is 8-1, Minnesota is 7-2, and kickoff is 8:20 p.m. ET. The app has it a pick'em — San Francisco by about a tenth of a point — while the market has the 49ers -3.5. Both quarterbacks are clear: Kirk Cousins for Minnesota, Brock Purdy for San Francisco.
Evans returning does not change the app's number. If your book has a 49ers price you like, Check it and let the app run it back through the model and the evaluator.
items.takeaway: Mike Evans returns tonight for San Francisco, not Tampa Bay — this morning had it wrong, and this brief corrects it. The app calls the game a pick'em against a market -3.5.

items.headline: The morning cards went 2-for-3
paragraphs: Balanced won. The Jets were +3 at -102, and they won outright, 27-24 at the Chargers. A dog winning outright covers every spread number on the board.
Value won too. The Giants were +6 at -109, and they won outright, 23-18 over Jacksonville at MetLife. The Giants led 20-6 at halftime and held on.

Hit Rate lost. The Jaguars moneyline was -255, the most likely winner on the board, and Jacksonville lost. That is the Hit Rate lane doing what it says: it picks the most likely winner, not a sure thing. The app gave Jacksonville about a 76 percent chance. The other 24 percent showed up.
Two wins and a loss is a good morning. Log the Jaguars loss the same way you log the two wins — the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself.
items.takeaway: Jets +3 won outright 27-24 and Giants +6 won outright 23-18. Jaguars moneyline -255 lost. Two of three cards won.

items.headline: Mayfield played hurt, and Detroit won anyway
paragraphs: Baker Mayfield played through the plantar fascia injury in his foot. He finished 20 of 33 for 187 yards and two touchdowns, both to rookie Ted Hurst, and he was sacked four times. Detroit won 31-21 and covered the 3.5.
The two-point move toward Tampa Bay during the week ended at Detroit -3.5, and the favorite still covered. Kansas City covered too, 34-7 over Arizona against a 15.5-point spread on DraftKings.

The big favorites did not all cover. Buffalo beat Miami 26-9 but did not cover 16.5. Chicago beat New Orleans 21-13 but did not cover 11.5. The app had Buffalo by about 3 and Chicago by about a quarter of a point — much closer to the final margins than the market was.
items.takeaway: Mayfield played hurt (20 of 33, 187 yards, 2 touchdowns) and Detroit still won 31-21, covering -3.5. Buffalo and Chicago won but did not cover their big numbers.

items.headline: Monday: both quarterbacks clear, injuries in the trenches and the backfield
paragraphs: Joe Burrow carries no injury designation after an illness and is expected to start for Cincinnati. Jayden Daniels is expected to start for Washington. The quarterback question is settled on both sides.

Cincinnati ruled out guard Dalton Risner with a knee injury. Guard Dylan Fairchild (oblique), safety Kyle Dugger (quadriceps) and cornerback Dax Hill (illness) are questionable. Washington has running back Rachaad White (heel), center Lucas Patrick (concussion) and cornerback Amik Robertson (ankle) questionable, plus running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), who has resumed practicing and is in line to return.
The inactives land about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. If White or Croskey-Merritt is out, Check the Washington price again — the number will move.
items.takeaway: Burrow and Daniels are both clear to start Monday. Risner is out for Cincinnati; White, Patrick, Robertson and Croskey-Merritt are questionable for Washington.

items.headline: One thing to know first: the evening board had not refreshed
paragraphs: The board refreshes every morning and evening, and this evening it had not refreshed by the time this brief was written. The numbers below are from the morning board, which is the latest available. Check the app for the latest before you bet.

Here is what the morning board says about the two games left. Tonight, the app has San Francisco winning by about a tenth of a point — a pick'em — against a market spread of -3.5. The app's total sits near 49.5 against a market total of 46.5. The app put no card on this game.

Monday, the app and the market nearly agree. The app has Cincinnati by about 5, the market has -6 on DraftKings and -5.5 on FanDuel. The app's total sits near 48 against a market total of 54.5. Again, no card on the game.

A gap is a starting point, not a bet. The card is what the model and the evaluator agreed on after the full check. If a number at your book catches your eye, type the line and the price into Check and let the app run it back through the model and the evaluator.
items.takeaway: The evening board had not refreshed, so these numbers are from the morning board — Check for the latest. The app calls tonight a pick'em and nearly agrees with the market on Monday. No card on either game.

items.headline: Hit Rate lost today, and that is the lane working as advertised
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win. It is not the pick most likely to profit. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate, and today showed why: Jacksonville had about a 76 percent chance, and the 24 percent happened.

Balanced is the middle ground — a strong pick without paying too much. The Jets were about a coin flip at +3, and they won outright. Value is always the model's plus-expected-value play. The Giants were barely over the line at +6, and they won outright too.
Three cards, three different jobs. Judge each one by its own job, not by whether it won today. A Hit Rate loss does not make the lane broken, and a Value win does not make it a lock next time.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate picks the most likely winner, not a sure thing — Jacksonville's 24 percent showed up today. Balanced and Value won outright. Judge each lane by its own job.

items.headline: The hook: why a half-point matters
paragraphs: A spread with a half-point in it — like -3.5 — has a name: the hook. The half-point exists so the bet cannot push. There is no tie. You win or you lose.

Here is a clearly labeled hypothetical example. Imagine a favorite listed at -3.5 at one book and -3 at another book, both at the same price. If the favorite wins by exactly 3, the -3.5 ticket loses and the -3 ticket pushes — your stake comes back. Same game, same price, different result, all because of the hook.

That is why shopping for the line matters as much as picking the side. A half-point is small until it is the whole bet. When you see two books a half-point apart, the better number is usually the one without the hook working against you — and Check will tell you what each price is actually worth.
items.takeaway: The hook is the half-point in a spread like -3.5, and it decides win, loss or push — a favorite winning by exactly 3 loses at -3.5 and pushes at -3, so shop the line.

items.headline: Cincinnati is up to -6, and the books disagree by a point
paragraphs: Washington opened at +4 and is now +6. Cincinnati is -6 on DraftKings at -114, -5.5 on FanDuel at -120, and -6.5 at Pinnacle. That is a full point of disagreement between books on the same game.
The move is toward Cincinnati, and it is a two-point move from the open. The app has Cincinnati by about 5, so the market has now moved past the app's number on DraftKings and Pinnacle.
If your book still shows Washington +6 or Cincinnati -5.5 and you like the look of it, Check it. A point of disagreement between books is exactly when Check earns its keep.
items.takeaway: Cincinnati moved from -4 to -6, and the books disagree by a full point: -5.5 on FanDuel, -6 on DraftKings, -6.5 at Pinnacle. Check your book's line.

items.headline: The hook is the story tonight
paragraphs: San Francisco is -3.5 on DraftKings and FanDuel, but -3.0 at Pinnacle. The hook is the difference between those two numbers, and tonight it is live: the app has the game a pick'em, so a 3-point 49ers win is a real possibility.

If your book shows San Francisco -3, that is a better number than -3.5 — same team, same game, and a win by exactly 3 pushes instead of losing. Check it before kickoff and let the app run it back through the model and the evaluator.
If your book only has -3.5, that is the price as it stands. Do not chase the -3 somewhere else after kickoff. The number you can actually bet is the only one that counts.
items.takeaway: San Francisco is -3.5 on DraftKings and FanDuel but -3.0 at Pinnacle. A 3-point win pushes at -3 and loses at -3.5 — check what your book has.

items.headline: The Jets-Chargers total flew over the morning number
paragraphs: The total dropped a full point in the morning, from 42.5 to 41.5. The game finished 27-24 — 51 points, ten over the morning total. The app's total sat near 46, closer to the final than the market was.
That is a result, not a signal. A total that already went over does not tell you anything about the next total. Note it, then move on to tonight and Monday.
items.takeaway: The Jets-Chargers total dropped to 41.5 in the morning and the game finished at 51 points. The app's total was near 46 — closer, but that is a result, not a signal.

items.headline: Tonight: check the hook, then Monday check the inactives
paragraphs: Two games left this week, and each one has its own check. Tonight, the check is the line: San Francisco -3.5 on the big books, -3.0 at Pinnacle. If your book has the -3, Check it before the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff in Mexico City.

Monday, the check is the inactives. They land about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, and that is when White, Patrick, Robertson and Croskey-Merritt get their final answer. Check the inactives, then Check your prices.

And one more thing: the evening board had not refreshed when this brief was written, so the numbers here are from the morning board. The board refreshes every morning and evening. Check the app for the latest before you bet anything tonight or Monday.
items.takeaway: Tonight, check whether your book has San Francisco -3 or -3.5 before the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. Monday, check the inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff, then Check your prices — and Check the app, since the evening board had not refreshed yet.
